passages.text: On the fourth day in Tripolis, then, Peter got up and found us awake. After greeting us, he went out to the water basin to wash and pray, and we followed his example. After we had prayed together and sat down before him, he spoke about the need to keep pure. When it was now daylight, he allowed the crowds to enter. Once the crowd had come in, he greeted many of them as usual and began to speak:

lexical_decisions.rationale: The noun denotes a place or vessel supplying water, not necessarily a modern bathroom. Washing precedes prayer.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸν περὶ τοῦ δεῖν ἁγνεύειν ἐποιεῖτο λόγον.
lexical_decisions.chosen: he spoke about the need to keep pure
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἁγνεύειν can concern ritual or moral purity; the discourse develops both and neither is excluded here.

passages.text: “Because of your great neglect of yourselves, your mind has sprouted the many harmful notions associated with religious worship, and you have become like land left uncultivated for lack of a farmer. You need much time for cleansing, so that your mind, receiving the true word imparted to you like good seed, may not choke it with evil thoughts and make it fruitless in the deeds that can save. Therefore those concerned for their own salvation must listen more continually, so that the wrongs multiplied over long periods may be brought into proportion, for cleansing, with the short time remaining through sustained .. effort. Since each person does not know the end of his own time, hurry to pull out the many thorns from your hearts, not little by little. For you will not be able to be cleansed that way, since you have lain uncultivated for so long.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὰς πολλὰς καὶ βλαβερὰς τῶν θρησκειῶν ὑπονοίας
lexical_decisions.chosen: the many harmful notions associated with religious worship
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains religious practices in the plural conceptual background; notions can also be suspicions or suppositions.
The supplied edition has two consecutive dots after συνεχεῖ. Exactly two dots remain in the main text; unavailable content is not restored.

lexical_decisions.chosen: may be brought into proportion, for cleansing
lexical_decisions.rationale: The proportionality concerns accumulated errors and the short remaining time, with sustained effort as means; the wording is not replaced by a claim of automatic cleansing.

source_issues.issue: The supplied text contains exactly two dots between the adjective and noun. They remain as two dots in English; no unavailable wording is reconstructed.

passages.text: You will not otherwise endure undertaking the great effort needed for your cleansing unless you become angry with yourselves and rebuke yourselves for the ways in which, like useless servants, you were ambushed by agreeing with your evil desires. Then you will be able to apply your righteous anger to your mind like fire to a field left uncultivated. So if you do not have righteous fire—I mean anger against evil desires—learn what good things you have been ambushed and deprived of, what punishment you have been prepared for, and by whom you have been deceived. In this way your mind, becoming clear-minded and kindled to anger like fire by the teaching of the one who sent us, may be able to burn things away in opposition to desire. Believe me: if you are willing, you will be able to set everything right.

lexical_decisions.rationale: Uses the POB servant gloss; the comparison retains the underlying bonded-status and master-accountability sense of δοῦλοι.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὰ κατὰ τῆς ἐπιθυμίας ἀναλῶσαι δυνηθῇ.
lexical_decisions.chosen: may be able to burn things away in opposition to desire
lexical_decisions.rationale: The supplied genitive τῆς makes κατά naturally against, not according to. The rendering takes the phrase as expressing opposition in the consuming action and leaves τὰ as general things; it does not silently turn the genitive into an accusative or specify an unprinted object. Alternatively the phrase may be construed as the things directed against desire, though this sits awkwardly in the fire-and-anger argument.

source_issues.source_quote: τὰ κατὰ τῆς ἐπιθυμίας ἀναλῶσαι δυνηθῇ.
source_issues.issue: The genitive construction is awkward in the stated argument. The English preserves opposition to desire without changing the case or inventing a specific object; an alternative formal grouping is the things against desire. The consuming action itself is secure, but the phrase’s exact grouping is uncertain.

passages.text: You are an image of the invisible God. Therefore those who wish to practice reverence must not say that idols are an image of God and that they must therefore be revered. For the human being is God’s image. Whoever wishes to show reverence toward God does good to a human being, because the human body bears God’s image. But not everyone bears the likeness: that belongs to the pure mind of a good soul. Nevertheless, since we know that the human being was made “according to the image and according to the likeness” of God, we tell you to show reverence toward this human being, so that the gratitude may be credited to God, whose image he is. You must therefore offer honor to God’s image—that is, the human being—in this way: food to the hungry, drink to the thirsty, clothing to the unclothed, care to the sick, shelter to the stranger, and visits and whatever help is possible to the prisoner. Not to speak item by item: whatever good things someone wishes for himself, let him likewise provide for another who needs them. Then a good reward can be credited to him for having shown reverence toward God’s image. By the same reasoning, if he does not undertake to do these things, he will be punished for having neglected the image.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὴν δὲ ὁμοιότητα οὐκέτι πάντες, ἀλλὰ ἀγαθῆς ψυχῆς ὁ καθαρὸς νοῦς.
lexical_decisions.chosen: But not everyone bears the likeness: that belongs to the pure mind of a good soul.
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the author’s image/likeness distinction rather than harmonizing them.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἵνα εἰς θεόν, οὗπέρ ἐστιν εἰκών, ἡ χάρις λογισθῇ.
lexical_decisions.chosen: so that the gratitude may be credited to God, whose image he is
lexical_decisions.rationale: χάρις can be gratitude, favor, or the benefit; gratitude is preferred in the transfer of honor to the one represented. The benefaction being reckoned as directed to God is another viable construal.

passages.text: What can it mean, then, to say that you revere every form for the sake of reverence toward God, when in every way you abuse the human being who truly is God’s image—murdering, committing adultery, stealing, and dishonoring him in many other ways? You ought not to do any evil that causes a person grief. But now you do everything that makes a person lose heart. For injustice and discouragement come through being murdered, having one’s property taken away, and all the other things you know you do not want to suffer. But you, deceived into evil by a certain malicious serpent through a notion of knowledge of many gods, show irreverence toward the true image—that is, the human being—while imagining that you show reverence toward insensible things.

lexical_decisions.rationale: ἑρπετόν is a creeping creature; serpent follows the recurring figure explicitly called ὄφις nearby without adding its identity as a name.

lexical_decisions.chosen: through a notion of knowledge of many gods
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the claim to knowledge and its many-gods qualification; it is not presented as the translator’s own true knowledge.
